subject: Post-call: Tool selection playbook + SDK/auth routing next steps
messages:
From: Kar⁠thik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Costa <elena@finovate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (tool selection, auth, routing)

Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC: 

Summary from call
- Finovate wants a low-latency document ingestion + question-answering flow for underwriting that includes: retrieval (embeddings + vector DB), optional reranker, and a function-calling layer to execute secure lookups (account status, KYC checks).
- Success criteria: <= 300ms median LLM latency on 512-token requests during a 50 qps burst, reranker improves precision@5 by >12%, and no sensitive doc content leaves Finovate VPC for PII datasets.

Redwood recommended architecture (short):
- SDK: server-side Node/Go SDK integrated in Finovate backend; recommend server-side auth with short-lived mTLS or OIDC tokens depending on your infra.
- Routing: primary -> hosted Redwood for dev/POC; Dedicated pool for perf tests; private deployment for production sensitive flows.
- Tool calling: two-layer approach: (1) fast internal tools for lookups (cache + DB) called synchronously, (2) external partner tools (credit bureau) invoked with async function-calling + callback/webhook.
- Embeddings & rerank: use 1536-dim embeddings (approx), index in managed vector store (Redis/Vector or Pinecone). Reranker: small cross-encoder model for cheap reordering, fall back to LLM-based reranking for edge cases.

Open items / asks for Finovate before POC
1) Confirm procurement/POC budget/contact (who handles procurement paperwork?)
2) Provide a redacted sample of 500 docs for ingestion sizing and embed perf testing (S3 link preferred).
3) Security questionnaire (we'll supply SOC2 evidence; please send yours).

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood: deliver integration playbook + scoping matrix (attached) and a runbook for auth options by Wed 7/7.
- Finovate: share sample data and procurement contact by Mon 7/5.
- Schedule 90-min POC kickoff (tech + security + procurement) w/in two weeks.

Attachments: redwood-integration-playbook.pdf (attached), scoping-matrix.csv

Thanks — I looped in Marissa and Monica for the technical lift.

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (technical notes + playbook excerpts)

Elena — quick technical notes to address the specific asks you raised. Kept bullets short so your eng team can skim.

1) SDK + auth options
- SDKs: Node, Go, Python officially supported. For low-latency server flows we recommend the server SDK and direct gRPC path where possible (lower overhead than REST).
- Auth: three flavors we support:
  * API keys (short-lived) for early POC (easy).
  * OIDC token exchange (recommended) for managed identity + role separation.
  * mTLS with customer certs (supported in Private/Dedicated) for strict network isolation.
- KMS/HSM: Yes — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and HSM (we provide integration docs for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault; HSM integration via PKCS#11 bridge).

2) Routing & deployment pattern
- Dev/POC: Hosted API (fast onboarding) with pinning to a small dedicated test pool for consistent perf.
- Staging: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) to replicate perf.
- Prod (sensitive): Private deployment inside your VPC with egress controls and private control plane.
- Policy example: route_by={latency: "<200ms"} fallback_to=smaller-model or cached-response on overload.

3) Tool / function-calling design patterns (examples)
- Tool definition (simple):
  {
    "name": "getAccountStatus",
    "input_schema": {"account_id": "string"},
    "output_schema": {"status": "enum[active,suspended]","last_checked": "iso8601"},
    "auth": "internal-token",
    "timeout_ms": 300
  }
- Tool choice: prefer internal DB/cache tools for high-frequency reads (fast + stable). Use external partner tool calls asynchronously (fire-and-forget with webhook/queue) or as a fallback.
- Parallel strategies:
  * Scatter-gather: invoke multiple rerankers or retrieval indices in parallel, aggregate top-K, then re-rank. Good when sources have orthogonal signal.
  * Race-with-fallback: start fast local index and concurrently a slower high-precision index; take the first acceptable response then cancel others.
  * Sequential waterfall: retrieval -> rerank -> tool-call, when steps have strong dependencies.

4) Error handling and resiliency
- Timeouts: enforce per-tool timeouts (150-500ms depending on SLA).
- Retries: idempotent reads may have 1 retry with exponential backoff; writes must be handled with safe dedupe tokens.
- Circuit breaker: trip after N failures for T seconds; fall back to cached responses or a degraded hallucination-safe stub.
- Observability: include per-tool latency, error-rate metrics and trace IDs; Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and per-route latencies for root-cause.

5) Embeddings & reranker recommendation
- Embeddings: 1536-dim (approx) vector per doc chunk; chunk size 512 tokens. Vector DB options: managed Redis vector or Pinecone. Use HNSW indexing for fast recall at scale.
- Reranker: start with a cheap cross-encoder (fine-tuned small transformer) to re-score top-50 candidates, then optionally run LLM-based re-rank (expensive) only on ambiguous queries. This hybrid reduces cost while preserving quality.

6) Practical POC scope suggestion (minimal):
- Ingest 5k doc chunks, index in Redis Vector, serve embeddings -> retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank -> LLM answer with function call for account lookup.
- Load test to 50 qps with realistic request distribution, track latency, precision@K.

I'll attach a short scoping CSV with knobs (attached). Happy to share a sample tool-definition repo after we lock scope.

--
